title: Changing a loading stylesheet link's rel leaves rendering blocked
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#link-type-stylesheet makes a parser-created `<link rel=stylesheet>` implicitly potentially render-blocking, so its fetch setup steps block rendering on it. Its process the linked resource steps unblock rendering only in their last step, but they can return early:

> If *el* no longer creates an external resource link that contributes to the styling processing model, or if, since the resource in question was fetched, it has become appropriate to fetch it again:
>
> 1. Remove *el* from *el*'s node document's script-blocking style sheet set.
> 2. Return.

So if script changes a parser-created `<link rel=stylesheet href=slow.css>`'s `rel` to something else before the response arrives, *el* stays in the render-blocking element set, and rendering stays blocked until *el* becomes browsing-context disconnected or the implementation-defined timeout passes. The [other unblock trigger](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#render-blocking) only covers a `blocking` attribute change.

Maybe unblock rendering on *el* in that early return when *el* no longer creates the external resource link (but not when it's being fetched again, since that fetch keeps it render-blocking).
